Defining quantum field theory complexity is challenging, yet it becomes significantly more tractable within the context of effective theories. Furthermore, our analysis indicates that a nonlocal mass-energy source should exhibit a nonlinearity in its gravitational field, effectively behaving as if there is an additional, independent source of gravity. We term this effect "ghost gravity," which arises directly from the inherent nonlinearity of general relativity itself.

Bipartite graphs are significant in many applications, leading to the development of specialized drawing techniques that optimize their structure clarity. Specifically, the authors present a polynomial-time algorithm designed to reduce crossings in a fixed layout: given a bipartite graph $G$, the method guarantees the creation of a drawing where every vertex-edge connection features bends with a maximum of nine 120-degree bends. Statistical significance testing, particularly the paired-permutation test, has been crucial for ensuring that performance differences observed between two natural language processing systems result in genuine findings and not mere chance. Our study introduces a universal linear-time metric designed to satisfy the requirements of a permutation test across all tasks processed by a specific configuration. Named the "Everything Is Great" (EIG) filter, this new measure ensures that performing a permutation t-test on every single prediction from a classifier—where a common practice when a task-specific metric is missing—yields a significance result. By integrating the U-Net architecture and the EIG filter, we developed a system capable of performing a permutation test on every prediction made by a specific configuration. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that the new U-Net configuration significantly outperforms standard approaches on the F1 score for the new U-Net architecture and the EIG filter, ensuring that performing a permutation t-test on every task is justified. This validation confirms that the new U-Net architecture and the EIG filter, which are designed to be used in conjunction with the U-Net configuration, are robust and reliable.

Pixel-level annotation is highly sought-after yet remains challenging to obtain, particularly within medical image segmentation, where a deep learning model's training relies on segmented images marked by expert knowledge.
